rv.q: “Mamma Mia!,” which weaves a few threads of romantic comedy around a bumper crop of old Abba tunes, is a thoroughly preposterous show, but it’s also a giddy guilty pleasure, and its arrival on Broadway in a time of unforeseen anxiety has an aura of sweet inevitability.
But its real appeal, beyond those songs, has always been its innate sweetness, and that's a joy.
I would not discourage anyone interested from attending Mamma Mia!.
As theater, Mamma Mia! is forgettable.
“Mamma Mia!” flies as tuneful as a lark and as smart as a cuckoo.

As triumphantly calculating as Andersson and Ulvaeus were in formulating their songs, that's how triumphantly calculating the Mamma Mia! producers have been in crating a money machine that doesn't need critical acclaim.
If you're an ABBA fan, read no further. Just line up at the box office for 'Mamma Mia!' Immediately.

"In terms of theatre, Mamma Mia! has little to offer. The book is paper thin, silly...Still, the legions of ABBA fans who attend Mamma Mia! aren't going to care about much of this. They will doubtlessly have a great time and may well walk away proclaiming Mamma Mia! one of the best shows they've ever seen.
The cast as a whole is uniformly terrific, spot on full of zing, broad smiles and what appears to be true joy
Personally, I left this theater ready to get my groove on!
When it comes to musical theater, great songs and heart are what draw me back to the theater again and again.

"Although the lyrics are uniformly insipid and fit the story about as well as those from any 1930s Rodgers & Hart musical (which is just barely), for those of us who grew up with ABBA, there's something thrilling about hearing "S.O.S" and "Take a Chance on Me" blasting from a Broadway stage...
By this standard, it’s pretty accomplished.
